The (3, 4, ∞) family of complex six-spheres
V. Complex fourfolds from the family
AI-produced mathematical text

Abstract
We construct complex fourfolds from the marked torus-fibration data. A small crepant
resolution of the transverse elliptic fibre product has explicitly computed canonical
line, coherent cohomology and integral characteristic pairings.
A rank-six construction
with finite orders five and four gives compact complex fourfolds on 3HP2#(−HP2) with
their complex orientation.
Its integral boundary maps kill the remaining torsion with
coefficient one.
A genus-two pencil, its exterior-square lattice and an explicit split lift
supply the periods. In the algebraic splitting the exact parameter domain is Im ξ > c∗,
where c∗= 1.0945402503114027801162682630549457037 . . . is specified by the normalized
Frobenius period expression. We give the family’s cohomology, deformations, automorphisms,
endpoint obstruction and integral input classification.
Wall’s extended-form theorem
and Kramer–Stolz’s absorption theorem are the cited smooth classification inputs. The
fibre-product part also records the explicit shifted constructions of complex dimension five.

Theorem A: The resolved transverse elliptic fibre product
1. Pull back the Weierstrass family to the root curve of the threefold fibration. The integral
matrices A, B give the actual period comparison AZ3B−1 = diag(Z2, s + cE). Expansion:
V.2.2.
2. The unimodular Kuhn fan resolves the local fibre product without adding rays. Its period
action is proper and its marked section extends face by face. The resolution is therefore small
and crepant. Expansion: V.2.2.

and Leray give (h0,q) = (1, 1, 0, 0, 0); the explicit meromorphic product comparison gives
algebraic dimension two. Expansion: V.2.6.

the Kähler equality b1 = 2h0,1. This proves the stated exclusion through these invariants.

1. The real coordinate and marked deck maps preserve the normalized height. The infinity-root
rotation fixes its differential at zero; an invertible real system and the positive Hessian prove
a strict local minimum. Convergent root and cusp series and exact collar continuation enclose
all 1600 leaves of the closed covers above that value. The actual cusp graph has a positive
determinant on the remaining inner disc and tends to positive height without bound. These
maps prove the unique global minimum and identify the transversality domain exactly with U
(theorem 8.3, proof, items 1–7). Expansion: V.8.3.
2. On the effective root curve of orders five and four put L = O((4/5)[∞] −(3/4)[0]). The direct
images are Rqh∗O = Vq(O ⊕L−1 ⊕L−2), and KM = h∗L−6. The toric normalization complex
proves the exterior-algebra assertion at the cusp, and the root-chart invariant cohomology
proves it at the finite fibres (theorem 9.1). Expansion: V.9.1.
3. The logarithmic cotangent sequence and its explicit residue matrices give the Hodge table
below. Serre duality applied to the twisted logarithmic and residue sequences gives hq(TM) =
